metric.debugger_profiler_support.TypeScr.summary: TypeScript/Node debugging and profiling is highly mature: both VS Code and WebStorm provide native source-level debugging via source maps and the standard V8/Node inspector protocol, and Chrome DevTools supplies an industry-standard CPU/memory profiler usable against any Node or browser TypeScript process. Score is slightly below the IDE metric because core debugging is mediated through source maps over the underlying compiled JavaScript (an indirection layer) and the bundled CLI inspector is explicitly documented as minimal, with richer functionality coming from the surrounding DevTools/IDE tooling rather than a single unified native TS debugger.

component_D_long_tail_editors.rationale: TypeScript has one of the widest documented sets of editor integrations of any language: an official Microsoft wiki catalogs support across Emacs, NeoVim, NetBeans, Notepad++, Sublime Text, Vim, Visual Studio, VS Code, WebStorm, Atom, and Eclipse, and a widely used community bridge (typescript-language-server) exposes tsserver over the standard Language Server Protocol so any LSP-capable editor (Neovim, Helix, Zed, Sublime via LSP, Emacs via lsp-mode/coc) gets rich TypeScript intelligence.

metric.ide_editor_support_quality.TypeSc.summary: TypeScript scores near the top of the rubric: it has an official Microsoft-maintained language service powering a first-party VS Code extension, a dedicated commercial IDE (WebStorm) with continuous investment, and one of the broadest documented sets of long-tail editor integrations of any language via both native plugins and the standardized typescript-language-server LSP bridge. A small deduction is applied for documented WebStorm large-project responsiveness/reliability complaints.

metric.debugger_profiler_support: A (0-25): Native, source-level (not just compiled-output) step debugger integration in the dominant general editor (VS Code).
B (0-25): Dedicated/commercial IDE debugger integration depth (conditional breakpoints, watches, remote/attach debugging).
C (0-25): Profiler tooling maturity -- CPU profiling, heap/memory snapshots, flamecharts, available via first-party or de-facto-standard tooling.
D (0-25): Breadth of third-party profiling/tracing tools building on a standard, widely adopted debug/profiling protocol.
metric.ide_editor_support_quality: A (0-25): Existence and maintenance quality of an official/first-party language server or IDE integration maintained by the language's steward.
B (0-25): Depth of support in the dominant general-purpose editor (VS Code) -- completion, diagnostics, refactoring, go-to-definition, rename-across-files.
C (0-25): Depth of a dedicated full-featured IDE (JetBrains-class) integration -- semantic navigation, refactors, debugging hooks, reported reliability.
D (0-25): Breadth of LSP-based or plugin-based support across long-tail editors (Vim/Neovim, Emacs, Sublime, Helix, Zed, Eclipse, NetBeans).
rubric.note: Frozen objective rubric to be applied identically to all 10 languages by their respective per-language shards. Each metric is decomposed into four equally-weighted 0-25 point components summing to a 0-100 normalized score.
rubric.observation_window: Evidence collected September 2026 from official Microsoft/TypeScript documentation, JetBrains WebStorm release blogs (2024-2026), Node.js/V8 inspector documentation, and third-party technical guides.
